LESSON: WILDLIFE AND TOURISM IN KENYA • WILDLIFE • HISTORICAL SITES • NATURAL SCENERIES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Wildlife and Tourism in Kenya • Wildlife • Historical Sites • Natural Sceneries
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Wildlife and Tourism in Kenya • Wildlife • Historical Sites • Natural Sceneries, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to conserve wildlife in our country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Wildlife and Tourism in Kenya • Wildlife • Historical Sites • Natural Sceneries together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: sharing what they have learnt as learners debate on the contribution of tourism to the economy of Kenya.

● Communication and Collaboration: speaking and signing clearly and effectively as learners brainstorm on and sign the difference

between a game reserve and a national park.

Values:
● Unity: team spirit as learners debate on the contribution of tourism to the economy of Kenya.

● Respect: respect self and others as learners visit a nearby tourist attraction site and write a report.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: work together as learners debate on the contribution of tourism to the economy of Kenya.

● Environmental Education: write an essay on the importance of museums as tourist attractions in Kenya.

Link to other subjects:

English and Kenyan Sign Language: as learner identifies, fingerspells and signs terms related to wildlife and tourism in Kenya

Suggested Learning Resources:

digital resources, print resources, resource person, local and extended environment, approved textbooks, KSL Dictionary,
